records.eligibility: Adults age 65 or older who live in the Tri-Cities; pre-registration is required and some fees vary by income.
records.access: Complete the eligibility assessment or contact SHARE reception.

records.description: A youth space offering wraparound support, outreach, peer connection and skill-building programs.
records.eligibility: Youth seeking a welcoming space and support; confirm current program details with the operator.

records.description: Advocacy and support concerning income assistance, disability benefits, federal income supports, tenancy, debt and housing stability.
records.eligibility: Program criteria vary; contact Sources to identify the appropriate advocacy or housing program.
records.access: Review the program page and call Advocacy Services for current intake.

records.name: Surrey housing and homelessness resource navigation
records.description: A current public guide to shelters, outreach, health services, housing resources and free BC 211 navigation for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
records.eligibility: People seeking Surrey housing or homelessness resources; individual programs set their own eligibility.
records.access: Use the current City guide or call BC 211 for free, confidential referral support.

records.name: Service BC government-service navigation
records.description: Front-line navigation for provincial services including B.C. birth certificates, health cards, BC Services Card identity verification and other government services.
records.eligibility: People seeking access to participating B.C. government services; availability varies by service and office.
records.access: Use the online service finder, contact centre or local office; confirm the needed service is offered before visiting.

records.name: New Westminster Crises Response Outreach Team
records.description: Person-centred outreach for people experiencing homelessness, mental-health or substance-use challenges, including help connecting to food, shelter, community services and identification such as BCID.
records.eligibility: People in New Westminster who may need help connecting to resources related to homelessness, mental health or substance use.
records.access: Call CRT Outreach Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., excluding holidays, or use the current City page for drop-in updates.

records.name: SHARE Food Bank
records.area_served: Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam and Port Moody
records.description: Food support for Tri-Cities individuals and families, with registration and distribution locations in Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam and Port Moody.
records.eligibility: Tri-Cities residents seeking food support. Registration requires government-issued identification and recent proof of address; the operator states that no means test is required.
records.access: Register in person without an appointment at the Port Moody food bank, or review the current operator page for community distribution locations and times.

records.name: StreetSMART
records.organization: City of Surrey, Surrey Libraries and Lookout Housing and Health Society
records.description: Trauma-informed street outreach and walk-in support connecting people experiencing homelessness with health services, shelters, supportive housing and other community supports.
records.eligibility: People experiencing homelessness in Surrey City Centre or Newton who need outreach or service connections.
records.access: Use the weekday outreach or walk-in hours listed on the City page, or contact the StreetSMART team by phone.

source.title: Housing & Homelessness Resources and Services — StreetSMART

records.name: Alouette Outreach Services
records.description: Outreach for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, with help replacing lost ID, accessing income assistance, navigating health and addiction services and finding housing or shelter.
records.eligibility: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Maple Ridge or Pitt Meadows; contact the operator to confirm the appropriate outreach pathway.
records.access: Call Alouette Addictions Services or use the current operator page to ask for Outreach Services.

records.name: Disability Planning Helpline
records.description: Free one-to-one help with disability benefits and planning, including the Canada Disability Benefit, Disability Tax Credit and Registered Disability Savings Plan.
records.eligibility: Anyone with a disability-related planning or benefit question, including disabled people, family members, friends and professionals.
records.access: Call, email or use the online form; the operator notes that response times can be longer during high demand.

records.name: Tax AID DABC
records.area_served: British Columbia remotely; in-person partners include Metro Vancouver and Fraser Valley
records.description: Free year-round help for people with disabilities on low incomes to file current or prior-year simple tax returns and connect with tax-related benefits.
records.eligibility: People with disabilities in B.C. whose yearly income is under the current program threshold; confirm that the return is within the program's scope.
records.access: Book an appointment online or call Tax AID DABC.

source.title: File Income Taxes — Tax AID DABC

records.name: Volunteer Income Tax Program
records.description: Year-round monthly volunteer tax clinics for Burnaby residents with low incomes and straightforward tax situations.
records.eligibility: Burnaby residents who meet the current household-income and tax-situation criteria and hold a Burnaby Neighbourhood House membership; fees can be waived for financial need.
records.access: Use the current pre-screening form and wait for the program to arrange an appointment.

records.name: Admin and Accounting Works
records.area_served: British Columbia; virtual program administered from Surrey
records.description: A free 12-week virtual program with office, bookkeeping, QuickBooks, job-search and work-practicum training.
records.eligibility: B.C. residents age 50 or older who meet the published work-status and immigration or work-authorization criteria.
records.access: Contact Empowered for Employment to confirm the next intake and complete screening.

source.title: Empowered for Employment — Admin and Accounting Works

records.name: Active Generation for Employment
records.description: Group occupational and job-search training with one-to-one coaching, follow-up and possible financial supports.
records.eligibility: Unemployed or precariously employed Metro Vancouver residents age 55 or older who meet the published work-authorization and labour-program criteria and face employment barriers.
records.access: Review eligibility and contact the program for current intake.

source.title: Active Generation for Employment for Job Seekers

records.name: BladeRunners
records.area_served: Lower Mainland, with current training listed in Surrey
records.description: Career exploration, certified skills training, work experience and job coaching for young people seeking employment.
records.eligibility: People age 15–29 who meet the program's published work-authorization, school-status, employment-search and language criteria.
records.access: Contact BladeRunners to confirm the next training and registration availability.

records.name: Indigenous Skills and Employment Training provider directory
records.area_served: British Columbia, including Lower Mainland providers
records.description: A directory of Indigenous Skills and Employment Training providers offering career support, training and, depending on the provider, help with tuition, equipment, transportation or living costs.
records.eligibility: Indigenous people; detailed eligibility and available supports are set by each provider and may be distinctions- or community-specific.
records.access: Use the official directory to find the appropriate provider and confirm program eligibility directly.

records.name: Travel Assistance Program
records.description: Discounts from participating carriers for eligible B.C. residents who must travel within the province for non-emergency specialist care not available locally.
records.eligibility: B.C. residents enrolled in MSP with an eligible referral to the closest available insured specialist service and no third-party travel coverage.
records.access: Ask the referring clinician for a TAP form, then obtain a confirmation number before booking travel; past travel is not reimbursed.

records.name: Medical transportation supplement
records.description: Assistance with extraordinary transportation costs for essential medical treatment for eligible recipients of B.C. income or disability assistance.
records.eligibility: Specified recipients of income assistance, disability assistance or Medical Services Only coverage, or people approved under the published life-threatening-need rules.
records.access: Contact the income or disability assistance program before travel to determine whether the supplement applies.

records.name: Hope Air travel support
records.description: Free flights and related travel supports for people who must travel long distances to provincially insured specialist appointments and face financial barriers.
records.eligibility: People with a confirmed, provincially covered specialist appointment requiring long-distance travel who demonstrate financial need; detailed travel requirements apply.
records.access: Apply online once the appointment is confirmed or call for help completing the application.

records.name: Medical Transportation Benefit
records.description: Financial support toward transportation, meals or accommodation when an eligible First Nations client must travel for medically necessary care unavailable in their community of residence.
records.eligibility: First Nations people with Indian status who live in B.C., and eligible infants under the current Health Benefits rules; coverage and prior-approval requirements apply.
records.access: Contact a Community Patient Travel Clerk or FNHA Medical Transportation assessor before travel to confirm eligibility and approval.

records.name: Volunteer Wheels
records.area_served: White Rock and South Surrey, with healthcare trips across Metro Vancouver
records.description: Volunteer door-to-door transportation for essential healthcare appointments for local residents who cannot use public transit and have no other transport.
records.eligibility: Residents of White Rock or South Surrey who cannot use public transit and have no other way to reach an essential healthcare appointment.
records.access: Request a ride at least one week in advance; the operator limits service to four drives per month and confirms each trip with the rider.
